page: OVHcloud r3-64 is a memory-optimized server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC processor with 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Storage is provided by a local 200 GB NVMe SSD, and the network interface delivers a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Additionally, the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core performance, with the stress-ng single-core CPU test and Geekbench single-core score both placing in the top 25% of tested servers. Memory performance is also notable, with the Passmark memory score and large-block memory write bandwidth of 101.05 GB/sec ranking in the top tier. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. The server demonstrates average throughput in database operations, Redis SET operations at 20.07 million operations per second, and static web serving at 8.61 GB/sec.

The r3-64 instance offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it a resource-dense option for memory-bound workloads. However, because it features single-threaded cores with one thread per core and lacks hyper-threading, its multi-core compute scaling is moderate compared to its strong single-core capabilities. This hardware profile is suited for memory-intensive applications such as in-memory databases, caching layers, text processing, and moderate-scale data processing tasks that benefit from dedicated CPU cores and high memory capacity without requiring massive parallel compute.
